proton irradiation of bubble-domain films causes a decrease in the mobility of domain walls and an increase in the damping of the ferromagnet resonance.
proton irradiation of bubble domain materials results in decreased bubble mobility.
the mobility of domain walls in rare-earth iron garnets is decreased by irradiation with 1-3 MeV pro-tons to fluences greater than ∼ 1015 p/cm2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of fast neutrons and protons on the mobility of bubble domains in rare-earth iron garnet thin films.
the effects of ionizing radiation on the magnetic domain wall motion in bubble domain garnet films.
the effects of ionizing radiation on magnetic bubble domain materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proton irradiation of bubble domain materials causes a significant increase in the magnetic damping, but no measurable change in the coercive force.
the mobility change is due to radiation damage in the garnets and that the damage is caused by the protons and not the electrons or neutrons.
proton induced radiation damage in magnetic bubble domain films results in an increase in the magnetic damping and a reduction of the mobility of the domain walls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proton damage to bubble-domain materials is primarily a radiation-induced mobility change.
the proton irradiations produce a damage which increases magnetic damping and decreases the domain wall mobility, but has little effect on the coercive field of the garnet films.
radiation-induced damage is observed in bubble-domain materials only at high fluences and high energies, and only when displacement damage occurs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bubble domain materials are sensitive to displacement damage.
the domain wall mobility in rare-earth iron garnet bubble domain films is sensitive to displacement damage induced by 3 MeV proton irradiations to fluences greater than 1016 p/ cm2.
the mobility of the domain walls in bubble domain films decreases by a factor of two when the films are irradiated with fast protons to fluence levels of 1016 p./cm2.
